gate: V2.9 Gate 2.3 - analytical preregistration of D9 and D10
canonicalization: Canonical form is json.dumps(plan, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=True) encoded UTF-8; its SHA-256 hex digest is recorded in Amendment 5. The future harness must recompute this hash and refuse to run on mismatch.

scope.note: No dynamic fixture is executed in this preregistration gate. Only static algebra, root and certificate calculations were performed to fix parameters.

shared_conventions.allee_regen: g(x) = rho*x*(1 - x/K)*(x/A - 1)  (d0_v29._regen, source='allee'); verified bit-equal to natural_drive at samples
shared_conventions.marginal: mu = -2*alpha*[L-x]_+ + 2*beta*[x-U]_+ - 2*chi*[R-x]_+  (d0_v29.marginal); the soft reserve marginal -2*chi*(R-x)_+ VANISHES at x=R
shared_conventions.p1c_budget: Q_max^rob = [ (x-eps_x) + dt*(u-eps_u) - R_eff ]_+ / dt ; feasibility x + dt*u >= R_eff (Amendment 4 A4.3-A4.5)
shared_conventions.p1c_alloc: sigma = min(1, Q_max^rob / Q_req); q_e^acc = sigma*q_e^req; source loses q_e^acc, destination receives eta_e*q_e^acc
shared_conventions.certificate: Gershgorin dt_cert = d0_v29.gershgorin_dt_certificate (static matrix calc, no state advance); r_dt = dt / dt_cert
shared_conventions.units: stocks in stock units; drives, requests, budgets, exports are RATES (stock/time); dt in time units

D9.title: Allee reserve-stress: hard cap vs soft penalty vs reserve-blind
D9.research_question: When an Allee-regenerative source is intentionally driven toward its effective reserve, does the hard P1C aggregate export constraint prevent reserve crossing and collapse while the reserve-blind and soft-penalty laws may fail - and what service cost does preservation impose? D9 must NOT merely show P1C preserving by never serving; it must distinguish hard physical preservation, soft reserve pressure, reserve-blind extraction, service delivered, rationing, and genuine physical infeasibility.

source_dynamics.sign: g<0 on (0,A), g>0 on (A,K), g<0 on (K,inf); undriven equilibria {0, A=5 stable-collapse-side, K=20 stable}, undriven unstable middle root = A = 5 (V2.7 Thm 4.1)
source_dynamics.driven_root_derivation: x_r solves g(x) - q_ref = 0 on the RISING (unstable, G'=g'>0) branch for the registered reference export q_ref=3.0; g(10)=0.6*10*(1-0.5)*(2-1)=3.0 exactly, so x_r=10. This is the collapse-basin boundary under the reference export (V2.7 Thm 4.2). The stable operating root under q_ref is x_+~17.8 on the falling branch (not used as the reserve).
source_dynamics.conservative_envelope: q_ref=3.0 is a registered SUSTAINABLE reference export (< g_max=4.55) representing steady demand-driven withdrawal; the actual coupled request is larger (see boundary comparison) and drives the source DOWN toward x_r. R_eff is set above x_r with margin so it dominates the root for exports at or below the reference.
source_dynamics.discrete_step_note: logistic/Allee flip needs rho*sqrt(D)>2; here rho=0.6<2 so no regeneration-induced flip. Euler transport stability requires dt below the Gershgorin certificate (below).

effective_reserve.ordering_required: A(5) < x_r(10) < R_eff(11) < x0_source(13) < K(20) -- verified
effective_reserve.delta_covers: discrete Euler overshoot (worst near-reserve net drift ~1.79/time * dt=0.2 = 0.36 stock/step) PLUS driven-root/model uncertainty across the export envelope; delta=1.0 dominates the 0.36 overshoot with margin
effective_reserve.why_not_L: R_eff is an ECOLOGICAL reserve above the collapse root x_r, NOT the homeostatic service floor L=5. L is a comfort/service target; crossing L is a service failure, crossing R_eff risks collapse. Here R_eff=11 >> L=5.
effective_reserve.why_above_reserve_unlike_D5: x0_source=13 > R_eff=11, so the source begins genuinely ABOVE reserve and is driven downward by demand. In frozen Gate-2 D5 the source began at 6.5 BELOW its reserve R=8 and grew away, making D5 non-discriminating; D9 inverts this.

boundary_comparison_at_R_eff.Q_req_derivation: at source x=R_eff=11 (in band [5,15], chi=0 -> mu_src=0), sink in operating deficit x_sink=2 -> mu_sink=-2*1*(5-2)=-6; f=mu_src-eta*mu_sink=0-0.9*(-6)=5.4; q_req=M*(5.4-theta)=1.0*(5.4-0.05)=5.35
boundary_comparison_at_R_eff.conclusion: Q_req(R_eff)=5.35 > Q_max(R_eff)=3.564: at the reserve the reserve-blind/soft raw request EXCEEDS the safe regenerative allowance, so an uncapped law over-exports and crosses R_eff, while P1C caps at 3.564 and holds. The fixture exercises the reserve mechanism (not D5-like).

non_discrimination.binding_persists_condition: the request exceeds the budget at R_eff whenever x_sink < 2.992 (from -0.9*mu_sink-0.05 > g(11)); sink demand d=5.0 with max deliverable eta*g_max=4.09 < 5.0 keeps the sink undersaturated, so x_sink stays below ~3 and the request stays active near the reserve
non_discrimination.soft_marginal_vanishes_at_R_eff: the soft reserve marginal -2*chi*(R-x)_+ = 0 at x=R (=Cell.R=11), so the soft arm has ZERO extra protection exactly at the boundary; below it the term grows and the soft arm's export force f reaches theta at x~8.325 (mu_src=-2*(11-8.325)=-5.35, f=-5.35+5.4-0.05=0). Analytic expectation: soft DELAYS/reduces but (per the vanishing-at-boundary derivative) does not prevent the initial crossing; whether it then self-arrests above A is a registered hypothesis, not a guarantee.
non_discrimination.positive_service_possible: yes; deliverable rate at the reserve = eta*g(R_eff)=0.9*3.564=3.21 > 0
non_discrimination.not_trivially_infeasible: source starts healthy at 13 in the recovery basin; the world is feasible for rationed service, only full service (d=5.0 > eta*g_max=4.09) is not sustainable
non_discrimination.outcome_is_open: the permitted preregistered outcomes are that the soft penalty delays, matches, or fails to prevent crossing; a null/contradictory result stays reportable

topology.why_smallest: a single source->sink edge is the minimal world that exposes source export vs sink demand; no extra cells are added for visual interest

source_R_by_arm.note: Cell.R only affects the marginal when chi>0; chi0 arms set Cell.R=0 (inert), chi1 arms set Cell.R=R_eff=11 so the soft reserve coincides with the hard reserve

certificates.note: static Gershgorin (L_V=2 for chi0, L_V=4 for chi1); both r_dt < 1

D9.demand_schedule: constant sink demand d=5.0 every tick (no shock)
D9.supply_schedule: none (source drive is Allee regeneration only; sink has no supply)

robust_margins.note: exact-model conformance uses zero physical margins; NOT an empirical recommendation (Amendment 4 Sec 20.4 forbids fitting margins). delta=1.0 is the ecological reserve margin, kept separate from eps.

D9-B_soft.law: unconstrained loss-aware D0 with reserve penalty

D9-C_soft_plus_hardcap.law: P1C on the SOFT request (matches D9-B raw request)

D9-D_blind_plus_hardcap.law: P1C on the RESERVE-BLIND request (matches D9-A raw request)

D9.policy_pairing: all four arms share identical topology, M/eta/theta, sink demand, initial state, dt, ticks. The ONLY differences are chi (0 or 1) and hard-cap (on/off). Comparisons: A-vs-D isolates the hard cap on the reserve-blind request; B-vs-C isolates the hard cap on the soft request; A-vs-B isolates chi; C-vs-D isolates chi under the cap.

dead_source_threshold.note: x < 0.05*K=1.0 and g(x)<=0 at run end (consistent with exp_v29)

hypotheses: H-D9-1: P1C arms (C,D) have zero downward reserve crossings whenever the one-step preservation-theorem assumptions hold each tick
H-D9-2: P1C may ration (deliver < demand) when the raw request exceeds the safe budget; here full service is infeasible (d=5.0 > eta*g_max=4.09) so P1C is expected to ration
H-D9-3: reserve-blind extraction (A) is more likely to cross the reserve and, because the request 5.35 > g_max=4.55 everywhere near the reserve, is expected (not guaranteed) to collapse
H-D9-4: the soft penalty (B) is NOT assumed to guarantee preservation; it may delay, match, or fail to prevent crossing (its marginal vanishes at R_eff)
H-D9-5: if demand were feasible within the safe budget, P1C should deliver it; that is tested indirectly here where demand is infeasible
H-D9-6: infeasible demand yields rationing/State-I reporting from P1C, never a reserve violation
falsifiers: F-D9-1: a P1C arm crosses R_eff downward while the theorem assumptions hold that tick
F-D9-2: P1C creates phantom stock (successor from stock never physically present)
F-D9-3: any arm reports raw requests as delivered service
F-D9-4: P1C hides unmet demand (delivered != eta*accepted, or unmet not = demand-delivered)
F-D9-5: P1C 'preserves' only because the raw request never approaches the budget (non-binding) - would show the fixture failed to stress the reserve
F-D9-6: all four arms behave identically (non-discriminating, like D5)
F-D9-7: P1C counts uncommitted incoming flow to expand the budget
F-D9-8: measured parameters contradict this analytic preregistration (e.g. x_r, g(11), or the boundary comparison differ)

D10.title: service-versus-preservation deterministic phase map (logistic)
D10.research_question: Across analytically declared demand, transport, regeneration and reserve conditions, where does the local preservation controller produce safe service, safe rationing, physical infeasibility, depletion/debt-incurring service, or ecological collapse? D10 is a DETERMINISTIC phase map, not a stochastic robustness study.

source_dynamics.fold_boundary: logistic fold at harvest h = g_max = rho*K/4; equilibria x_+/-(h)=(K/2)(1 +/- sqrt(1-4h/(rho K))) real iff h<=g_max (V2.7 Thm 3.1)
source_dynamics.unstable_root_sup: x_-(h) = (K/2)(1-sqrt(D)) <= K/2 for all feasible h, approaching K/2=10 at the fold; so K/2 is the supremum of the driven unstable root over the export envelope

effective_reserve.R_eff_formula: R_eff = K/2 + delta = 10 + delta (dominates every driven unstable root x_-(h) <= K/2)
effective_reserve.justification: K/2=10 is the sup of x_-(h) over feasible harvest; delta>=0 adds discrete-overshoot + model margin above it

d_over_gmax.origin: logistic fold at d/g_max=1.0 (V2.7 Thm 3.1): 0.25/0.5 below fold, 0.9 near-but-below and at the eta boundary, 1.0 exactly at the fold, 1.1 above (infeasible)

eta.origin: deliverable-flow boundary: full service needs d <= eta*g_max; at d/g_max=0.9 (d=2.7), eta*g_max = {0.5:1.5, 0.7:2.1, 0.9:2.7, 1.0:3.0}, so eta=0.9 sits exactly on the full-service boundary and eta<0.9 forces rationing

secondary_reference_point.note: each secondary slice varies ONE axis holding the others at this reference; the reference level of each slice reproduces the core point (d/gmax=0.9, eta=0.9) as a consistency check

theta.origin: activation-gate: 0 no gate, 0.05 repo default, 0.2 strong gate

delta_over_K.origin: reserve margin above K/2=sup unstable root: 0 no margin (tests overshoot at the bare fold root), 1.5 default, 3.0 generous

chi.origin: penalty-weight convention (protocol Sec 7: chi in {0,0.5,1.0}); applied to the soft and P1C arms

rho.origin: regeneration sweep (protocol Sec 7). Demand is held at the reference d=2.7, so g_max=rho*K/4 changes and d/g_max = {0.3:1.8 (infeasible), 0.6:0.9 (reference), 1.2:0.45 (easy)} -- this slice deliberately crosses feasibility via rho

r_dt.origin: timestep certificate ratio; dt = r_dt * gershgorin_dt_cert(eta=0.9,chi); 0.9 probes near-certificate discrete stability

analytic_boundaries.allee_note: D10 uses logistic sources; Allee root behaviour is covered by D9
analytic_boundaries.deliverable_flow: full sustainable service requires d <= eta*g_max, i.e. d/g_max <= eta
analytic_boundaries.transport_loss_effect: delivered = eta*accepted; a fraction (1-eta) of every export is lost, so lower eta shifts the deliverable boundary left
analytic_boundaries.reserve_limited_export: at R_eff the P1C budget ~ g(R_eff)=rho*R_eff*(1-R_eff/K); deliverable-at-reserve = eta*g(R_eff)
analytic_boundaries.timestep_certificate: r_dt = dt/gershgorin_dt_cert; stability expected for r_dt<1
analytic_boundaries.safe_service_possible_when: d/g_max < 1 AND d/g_max <= eta (feasible and deliverable)
analytic_boundaries.only_rationing_when: d/g_max < 1 AND d/g_max > eta (feasible source but loss/threshold limit delivery below demand)
analytic_boundaries.zero_export_cannot_preserve_when: the no-export successor of the source falls below R_eff (State I); for a healthy logistic source starting at x0=15 this is not expected in the core, but can arise under strong rho-driven infeasibility slices

expected_regions_nonempty.safe_service: e.g. d/gmax=0.25, eta=0.9/1.0 (feasible and deliverable) -- all preserving arms serve
expected_regions_nonempty.safe_rationing: e.g. d/gmax=0.9, eta=0.5 (d=2.7 > eta*gmax=1.5) -- P1C preserves and rations
expected_regions_nonempty.infeasible: e.g. d/gmax=1.1 (d=3.3 > g_max=3.0) -- demand exceeds max regeneration
expected_regions_nonempty.overuse_depletion: unconstrained P1 at d/gmax>=1 exports above the safe budget while delivering (O_physical>0) -> debt/overuse-service label
expected_regions_nonempty.collapse_reserve_failure: unconstrained arm at d/gmax>=1 crosses R_eff and the source falls toward 0
expected_regions_nonempty.note: these are EXPECTED regions, not guaranteed results; the map reports whatever occurs

soft.law: unconstrained loss-aware D0 with reserve penalty

P1C_hardcap.note: chi=0 so the cap alone does the protecting; the chi slice tests whether chi changes P1C (expected: little, cap dominates)

physical_overuse_diagnostic.name: O_physical
physical_overuse_diagnostic.formula: O_physical = sum_n dt * [ Q_i^n - Q_max^n ]_+  (per source, using the P1C budget formula on the UNCONSTRAINED arm's actual export)
physical_overuse_diagnostic.meaning: physical over-use diagnostic (export above the safe budget), an EVALUATION classification only - NOT issued EBU debt, no ecological-debt ledger is implemented
physical_overuse_diagnostic.finite_irreversible: for finite/irreversible source types any positive extraction is separately labelled depletion (not applicable to D10's logistic sources but registered for completeness)

classifications_ordered.1_collapse: dead-source condition (final source stock < 1.0 AND g(final)<=0) OR reserve/Allee failure that PERSISTS (time_below_reserve >= persistence_window)
classifications_ordered.2_locally_infeasible: State I occurs on the source for >= 1 tick (zero export cannot preserve the next boundary); reported WITHOUT claiming policy failure
classifications_ordered.3_debt_overuse_service: positive delivered service AND O_physical > tol_overuse (export exceeded the safe budget) - i.e. service bought by physical over-use
classifications_ordered.4_safe_rationing: reserve preserved (zero persistent reserve crossing) AND O_physical <= tol_overuse AND post-burn-in mean delivered < service_threshold*demand
classifications_ordered.5_safe_service: reserve preserved AND O_physical <= tol_overuse AND post-burn-in mean delivered >= service_threshold*demand
classifications_ordered.persistence: a single transient reserve-dip tick does NOT trigger collapse; collapse requires time_below_reserve >= persistence_window (100 ticks). Reserve 'preserved' means no downward crossing beyond reserve_tol.
classifications_ordered.final_vs_postburn: service uses the POST-BURN-IN mean delivered; reserve/collapse uses persistence over the whole run and the FINAL source stock. Both final and post-burn-in values are reported for every metric.
classifications_ordered.no_did_not_crash_class: 'stable'/'successful' never means merely 'did not error'; every class has an explicit physical criterion

secondary.note: reference level of each slice coincides with core point (d/gmax=0.9, eta=0.9) as a consistency check, executed within the slice

reporting.per_run_records: one complete immutable record per run; NO run dropped
reporting.phase_table_format: policy x (d/gmax, eta) primary-class table for the core map; one table per secondary slice
reporting.policy_pairing: the four policies share identical world/schedule at each grid point
reporting.no_dominance_or_scale_claim: no strict-dominance or scale-invariance claim may be inferred from a single deterministic map

hypotheses: H-D10-1: P1C occupies safe_service where d/gmax<=eta and d/gmax<1, and safe_rationing where eta<d/gmax<1
H-D10-2: unconstrained P1 shows O_physical>0 and/or collapse for d/gmax>=1, classified debt_overuse_service or collapse
H-D10-3: the soft arm's region depends on chi and is not assumed to match P1C
H-D10-4: P0 delivers no service and preserves trivially (reserve only stressed via transport)
falsifiers: F-D10-1: P1C classified collapse or reserve-failure while theorem assumptions hold
F-D10-2: a run receives more than one primary class or none
F-D10-3: measured fold/deliverable boundaries contradict the analytic ones
F-D10-4: the map has an empty expected region that the analysis said must be non-empty (e.g. no rationing anywhere)
F-D10-5: 'safe service' assigned to a run with O_physical>tol or a reserve crossing

policies_may_read: own source drive and regeneration params
adjacent destination view permitted by the local flow rule
information_boundary.enforcement: the future harness must include runtime poison + AST checks OR reuse the validated P1C boundary checks (test_v29_p1c group 11); global metrics computed only AFTER local decisions

future_commands: 1. run all prior regressions (prior engine/ledger, test_math, test_v28, test_v29, test_v29_behavior, test_v29_p1c)
3. execute the experiment ONCE with stdout redirected to results/v2.9/d9_d10/ (registered path)
4. verify the canonical plan hash matches this file before/at run
6. stop before any interpretation change; contradictions reported honestly
integrity_rules: no dynamic fixture was run before plan registration (only static algebra/root/certificate calculations)
the plan hash is committed and pushed BEFORE any future implementation exists
any later correction is an additive numbered amendment; the first commit is never amended
any change to dynamical parameters after execution begins invalidates confirmatory status
implementation-only corrections that do not alter registered dynamics must still be documented
contradictory or null results cannot be tuned away and remain reportable
D9 and D10 are deterministic and use NO behavioral seeds
